title: Phase-Modulated Hypergraph Fusion for Domain-Adaptive Seismo-Volcanic Event Classification in Andean Volcanoes
content: Cross-domain transfer of seismo-volcanic classifiers across geologically distinct volcanic systems remains a critical challenge: models trained on one volcano degrade when deployed at a new site without target-domain labels. This work proposes the Phase-Modulated Hypergraph Fusion (PMHF) model, a trimodal deep architecture that jointly exploits CLIP-encoded spectrograms, waveform images, and physics-informed seismic features to discriminate Long-Period (LP) from Volcano-Tectonic (VT) events in an adaptation domain setting. PMHF integrates three novel modules: a Spectral Calibrated Physics Gate (SCPG) that recalibrates tabular features via class-conditional resonance matrices; Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutions (DHGC) that propagate visual features through probability-conditioned hyperedges; and a Trimodal Episodic Cross-Attention (TECA) mechanism that fuses all pairwise modal interactions through persistent memory. Three leave-one-volcano-out scenarios evaluated across Galeras, Cumbal, and Chiles-Cerro Negro (bootstrap N=1000) show that PMHF achieves mean balanced accuracy 0.765, peaking at 0.868±0.009 (MCC =0.743±0.017) for Galeras+Cumbal→Chiles-Cerro Negro, where bimodal baselines plateau below 0.659 and tabular models exhibit systematic class inversion (MCC =−0.405). Domain adaptation diagnostics confirm that trimodal fusion achieves the tightest and most stable source-target feature alignment, enabling robust volcanic monitoring without retraining.
